# bankML

> Verified low-bit inference for the CPU you already have. A zero-dependency Rust runtime for 1-bit (Q1_0), ternary
> (Q2_0_g64) and F16 GGUF models whose kernels, forward pass, tokenizer, templates, samplers and grammars are checked
> against llama.cpp b11192's compiled code: bit-exact where ggml computes, token-identical where llama-server answers.
> `bankml serve` refuses to start unless the model file passes a header guard and matches its sha256 pin, speaks
> OpenAI's API and Ollama's, and puts a receipt (model, request and response sha256) on every answer.
> Licence: MIT OR Apache-2.0. Authors: Professor Codephreak and Gregory L. Magnusson (cryptoAGI).

This file is for language models and agents. The method below is the one the maintainers run on every release from a
fresh `git clone` of the live repository; each command was run as written. Follow it in order. Stop at the first step
that fails and report its output: bankML refuses with a reason rather than degrade.

## Method: from a fresh clone to a verified answer

Requirements: Linux x86_64 with AVX2 (the fast kernels are chosen at run time; scalar paths otherwise), git, curl,
Rust 1.99 (pinned by `rust-toolchain.toml`; rustup installs it), Python 3.10+ for the model importer. No root.

1. Clone and build.
   ```sh
   git clone https://github.com/cryptoagi/bankml bankML && cd bankML
   cargo build --release --locked
   ```
2. Test (offline; expect `test result: ok` lines and no `FAILED`).
   ```sh
   cargo test --release --locked
   target/release/bankml version
   ```
3. Get a model, verified and pinned. The importer downloads a catalogued model at a fixed revision, refuses it unless
   its sha256 is the published one, and writes its pin (`~/.local/share/bankml/forks/<file>.FORK.json`).
   ```sh
   python3 sAGI/models.py catalog                 # what can be imported, and whether it fits this machine
   python3 sAGI/models.py import bonsai-1.7b      # 248 MB, 1-bit; bonsai-8b (1.16 GB) and ternary-bonsai-8b (2.31 GB) also
   ```
4. Verify the file: the guard, then the sha256 pin, as one gate. Expect `"verdict": "play"` and exit code 0.
   ```sh
   target/release/bankml verify .models/Bonsai-1.7B-Q1_0.gguf \
     --fork ~/.local/share/bankml/forks/Bonsai-1.7B-Q1_0.gguf.FORK.json --json
   ```
5. Serve it from bankML's own forward pass (loopback only; it hashes the model before it binds the port).
   ```sh
   target/release/bankml serve .models/Bonsai-1.7B-Q1_0.gguf \
     --fork ~/.local/share/bankml/forks/Bonsai-1.7B-Q1_0.gguf.FORK.json --native --ctx 2048 &
   curl -s 127.0.0.1:18093/bankml          # what was verified: "verified": {"verdict": "play", "model_sha256": …}
   ```
6. Ask it. Every POST needs `Content-Type: application/json` and a loopback `Host`.
   ```sh
   # OpenAI's API
   curl -s 127.0.0.1:18093/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Name three primary colours."}],"max_tokens":24,"temperature":0}'
   # Ollama's API, with a JSON schema and a repetition penalty
   curl -s 127.0.0.1:18093/api/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"model":"bonsai-1.7b-q1_0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Name a cat."}],"stream":false,
          "options":{"temperature":0,"num_predict":24,"repeat_penalty":1.3},
          "format":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"}},"required":["name"]}}'
   ```
   The first answers with text and a top-level `bankml_receipt`; the second with `{"name": …}` in `message.content`.
7. Check an answer: `bankml_receipt.response_sha256` is the sha256 of the answer text exactly as the model produced it,
   and `model_sha256` names the weights that answered. Recompute the first to confirm the text you hold is the text
   the engine produced.
8. Read what bankML measured (0.3.7, the next release, not yet tagged; on 0.3.6 skip steps 8 and 9): `GET /bankml/metrics` (each answer's time to first token, prompt and generation
   tokens per second, energy per token when measured) and `GET /bankml/usage` (CPU, memory, each GPU's busy share and
   memory, package watts when measured). A value that was not measured is `null`; do not substitute an estimate.
9. Talk to bankML as itself, with its measurements in view: `python3 sAGI/console.py`, then http://127.0.0.1:7875.

## What bankML refuses, and why

- A model file that fails the guard or whose sha256 differs from its pin: it never loads.
- A sampler or option it does not reproduce exactly (e.g. mirostat, a custom sampler order, top-k outside 1–128): a
  400 with the reason, never an approximation. 0.3.6 reproduces top-k, top-p, min-p, temperature and the penalties;
  0.3.7 (next) the whole of llama-server's default sampler chain.
- A prompt longer than the context (`--ctx`): from 0.3.8 (next), a 400 with llama-server's
  `exceed_context_size_error` body, which names both counts.
- A non-loopback `Host`, a POST without a JSON `Content-Type`: 403 and 415.
